newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Some buyers in March OEX seen.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Some buyers in March OEX seen.

text.p: A few aggressive investors were buying up select March calls and puts on the S&P 100 index even though they go off the boards today and expire on Saturday, traders said Friday.

"We had good-size put buyers and call buyers of the expiring options," said Jack Callahan, an independent market maker in the OEX. "There were a number of opening positions. They're expecting volatility in the afternoon."
Traders said the OEX March 760 calls and 770 puts were the two main ones being bought.
By about 1200 CST/1800 GMT, the March 760 call had traded 10,760 contracts and the 770 put had traded 7,250.
Traders said the expectation of afternoon volatility was not surprising since the market has had a tendency lately to make dramatic moves in the last couple of hours of trading.
"I can understand why they draw that conclusion," Callahan said.
One OEX trader said volatility was high off the opening but quickly dropped.
The Chicago Board Options Exchange's (CBOE) volatility index, which is priced off select OEX puts and calls, was down 1.60 points, or about 6.75 percent, at 22.16.
The underlying OEX was up 1.43 at 764.30 and the spot S&P 500 index was up 3.27 at 785.92. June S&P 500 futures were up 5.15 at 793.55.
One firm said June S&P 500 fair value was at 7.10 points premium to cash, with buy programs at 8.25 points premium or wider and sell programs at 5.75 points premium or narrower.
March SPX options went off the boards Thursday and settled Friday morning on the opening of the spot index.
Volume was heavy in the OEX near-the-money calls and puts ahead of the expiration.
THe March 755 put traded more than 15,000 contracts, the March 760 put traded 19,850, and the March 765 put traded nearly 15,000.
Among the calls, the March 760 traded 11,200, the 765 traded 19,580 and the 770 traded about 20,200.
Traders said activity in the April series was relatively slack, with options selling being the most evident strategy seen.

Lawrence McMillan, who publishes the Daily Volume Alert, said in a report that the OEX expiration bias could be on the sell side because through Thursday, there were 55,000 more in-the-money puts open than calls.
"That augurs for sell programs on the close," he said.
